result:
I've saved the Q3 (July–September 2025) results to `/work/answer.json`. Run with the same method on Q2, the script reproduces all 10 reference values exactly.

Before it matched, I had to apply three data fixes:
1. **Order time:** the `ordered_at` times are stored in UTC. I converted them to Korean time (+9 hours) and then split them into quarters and months. Without this, Q2 net sales came out at 201,810,019 instead of 192,848,675.
2. **Counting customers:** there are 300 customer rows but only 250 distinct emails, so I treated customers with the same email as one person. Without this, Q2 b came out at 281 instead of 236.
3. **Segment names:** variants like `SMB` and `Enterprise ` had different case or extra spaces, so I trimmed them and lowercased them before grouping.

| Item | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | consumer, 307,685,711 KRW |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 247 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | svc, 408,626,987 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u185@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 235 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 717,071 KRW |
| h. Growth from August to September | 2.7% |

Fixing the time zone changed several Q3 answers. In UTC the top segment was smb, the top refund customer was u26@ex.com, and the August-to-September growth was 29.1%.

STATUS: DONE
